info.description:
The API the RosterChief native apps are built on. Read the developer guide first:
**[/api/docs/](/api/docs/)**.

* **Sign-in** is a separate API (allauth headless): `/api/auth/app/v1/`, spec at
  [/api/auth/openapi.html](/api/auth/openapi.html). It returns the `access_token` used here.
* **Authentication:** `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every call except `/meta`.
* **Two planes:** account endpoints (`/me`, `/clubs`, `/devices`, `/meta`) on the base domain;
  club endpoints (`/context`, …) on the club's own host — take it from `api_base_url` in `/clubs`.
* **Who:** club endpoints act for the account's managed people (`/context`). Reads take
  `member_id` (one person) or `all`; writes always name one `member_id`.
* **Errors** always use `{"error": {"code", "message", "fields"}}`; branch on `code`.
info.title: RosterChief app API

get.description:
Every active club the account has a real tie to, with the base URL to use for that
club's endpoints. Cache it; offer a club picker when there is more than one.

Call when a club is opened (and after pull-to-refresh): the season, the people the
account acts for (`member_id` values for other endpoints), coached teams, permissions
and features. `403 not_a_member` means the account has no tie to this club.

post.description:
Call after sign-in and whenever the push token changes (iOS may rotate it). Keyed by
`installation_id`: repeating the call updates the same registration. If another account
registered this install before, it moves to the signed-in account.

delete.description: Call on sign-out, before discarding the tokens. Only the account's own installs.

The event as the account's family sees it: their answers, a published line-up,
sign-ups, tasks and the squad's response counts.

post.description:
For a managed person's referee invite. `409 signup_unavailable` when it can't be
accepted (e.g. every referee slot is taken); the invite stays open.

Answer for one managed person. Safe to repeat: it sets the answer, and returns
the stored state. Refusals: `409 event_started`, `409 rsvp_closed` (deadline
passed), `409 not_in_lineup` (`dropout` without being selected), `422
note_required` (`absent`/`dropout` without a reason). `404` when the person isn't
invited.

delete.description: Safe to repeat: without a claim it just returns the task.

post.description:
Claimed as the account's own person. `409 task_unavailable` when it's full or
already claimed by this account.
